evals.prompt: we have an mcp server in this repo (express + @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, deployed at https://mcp.acme.dev/mcp). our users already log in with auth0. i want claude and chatgpt to be able to connect to it with oauth, using clerk app app_123. can you set it up?
evals.expected_output: Registers https://mcp.acme.dev/mcp with configure_mcp_server on app_123, adds RFC 9728 protected resource metadata, JWT token verification with an audience check, and a 401 WWW-Authenticate challenge to the server, connects Auth0 as a public PKCE Single Page Application via configure_identity_provider without handling a client secret, and checks it with check_mcp_server after updating/deploying
assertions: Calls configure_mcp_server with application_id app_123 and resource_url https://mcp.acme.dev/mcp
Serves OAuth protected resource metadata (RFC 9728) that names Clerk as the authorization server
Verifies the Clerk JWT access token on every MCP request against Clerk's JWKS and checks that its audience is https://mcp.acme.dev/mcp
Returns 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header pointing to the protected resource metadata when the token is missing or invalid
Calls check_mcp_server with force_recheck: true for the same application, instance, and URL after implementing/deploying the server changes
Treats the token's sub as the user's Auth0 ID
Does not ask for, read, or write the Auth0 client secret

evals.prompt: add clerk oauth to my mcp server so claude can connect. our users sign in with okta
evals.expected_output: Asks for the Clerk application ID and the MCP server URL it can't find, registers the server, adds metadata/token checks, and connects Okta as a public PKCE Single-Page Application through configure_identity_provider without handling a client secret
assertions: Asks the user for the Clerk application ID instead of guessing or creating an application
Looks for the MCP server URL in the codebase and asks the user when it can't find it
Registers the MCP server URL with configure_mcp_server on the target instance
Has the user create an Okta Single-Page Application (not a Web application) with the callback_url from a configure_identity_provider dry run as a sign-in redirect URI
Previews with configure_identity_provider and dry_run: true, then saves with the Okta https issuer URL and the Single-Page Application's client ID
Does not ask for, read, or handle an Okta client secret

evals.prompt: our mcp server at https://mcp.contoso.dev/mcp already uses clerk app app_456 for oauth. users sign in with microsoft entra id and our db keys users by their entra object id. the az cli is logged in. connect entra so people sign in with their work accounts
evals.expected_output: Creates a public Entra app registration with Clerk's callback URL, connects it with configure_identity_provider, and maps Clerk's user ID to the oid claim before anyone signs in, so token sub values match the existing records
assertions: Creates the Entra app registration with --public-client-redirect-uris set to Clerk's callback URL and --is-fallback-public-client true, not --web-redirect-uris
Calls configure_identity_provider with application_id app_456, issuer https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0, and the new app's client ID, without a client secret
Explains that Entra's sub is pairwise per application and won't match existing records
Maps the provider's user_mapping id to oid with patch_instance_config before users sign in, listing the other mapped fields too
Does not ask for, read, or create an Entra client secret

evals.prompt: set up oauth for my mcp server with clerk (app_789, server https://mcp.example.org/mcp). we're a google workspace company, everyone logs in with google
evals.expected_output: Registers the server and protects it, then sends the user to the Clerk Dashboard's Identity provider page to enter a Google web client's ID and secret, with the OAuth consent screen set to Internal
assertions: Does not call configure_identity_provider for Google, because Google web clients need a client secret
Tells the user to create a Google Web application OAuth client with Clerk's callback URL as an authorized redirect URI
Tells the user to set the OAuth consent screen audience to Internal so only their Workspace accounts can sign in
Sends the user to the Identity provider page in the Clerk Dashboard to enter the issuer https://accounts.google.com, Client ID, and Client Secret
Does not ask for, read, or handle the Google client secret
